questions.prompt: A woman wakes up centuries later in a decaying underground science facility and is guided by a moron in a robot ball who accidentally becomes a genocidal tyrant the moment he gets a body. Along the way she teams up with her old testing-chamber nemesis, now living in a potato, to take him down.
hints: The facility used to be run by a man obsessed with lemons and the moon.
Turrets that sing opera try to kill you.
The ending involves being launched into space on the moon, sort of.

questions.prompt: A young woman climbs a mountain that's secretly trying to kill her, while arguing with a shadowy version of herself who keeps showing up to tell her she's not good enough.
hints: There's a talking dragonfly-like camera drone who becomes your best friend.
You can dye your hair a different color mid-air to represent extra jumps.
The mountain has its own concerning weather patterns tied to how the story is going.

questions.prompt: A child falls into a hole and discovers an entire underground civilization of monsters who really just want to go back to the surface, including a goat mom, a skeleton who tells bad jokes, and a fish woman in armor who keeps mistaking you for a murderer.
hints: You can choose to befriend literally everything, including your own executioner.
A talking flower turns out to be the actual final boss in most endings.
Your choices are remembered even if you restart the game.

questions.prompt: A guy makes a deal with a forbidden voice in a temple to bring his dead girlfriend back, and the price is hunting down sixteen giant, mostly peaceful creatures and murdering them one by one with a sword and a horse.
hints: Climbing the monsters is basically the entire combat system.
There are basically no other enemies in the whole game except these sixteen.
The ending twist involves the guy slowly turning into the villain he was working for.
